text:
alyssa: Hey team — Acme Prod on dedicated pool dp-4 is seeing persistent 429s and tail latency spikes this morning. Started ~08:12 UTC. Token-level metric shows KV eviction rate skyrocketing.

alyssa: Quick snapshot from their runtime logs: 
```
[2026-03-05T08:12:34Z] tenant=acme-prod pool=dp-4 model=redwood-v1-large seq_len=48k kv_evictions=1247 evict_rate=3.2/s kv_free=1.1GB kv_total=12.0GB frag=38% error=throttle_kv_cache(429)
```

alyssa: They report a mix of long-context summarization jobs and normal chat traffic. Looks like long requests are forcing repeated KV evictions and causing other tenants to hit throttles.

ops-bot: Alert: Dedicated pool dp-4 high kv_eviction_rate for tenant acme-prod — threshold breached. Incident auto-created: INC-4321 :rotating_light:

sam: Thanks Alyssa. Can you grab a couple of repro requests (anonymized) and the recent /metrics scrape for dp-4? Also which model variant + quantization are they pinned to?

alyssa: Sending sample (sanitized) shortly. They pinned `redwood-v1-large-int8` and are sending batch jobs with context ~45k tokens. Repro payload (sanitized):
```
POST https://dedicated.redwood/api/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "redwood-v1-large-int8",
  "input": "<~45k tokens>...",
  "max_tokens": 2048
}
```

mike: Thanks. Two quick checks from infra:
1) run node-level kv stats on the host serving acme-prod: `curl http://node-metrics:9200/kv_stats?pool=dp-4&host=HOSTNAME`
2) check allocator free lists: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-heap-inspect --host HOSTNAME`

mike: Typical signatures: high fragmentation + repeated small frees when long ctxs churn the KV caches. Fragmentation % > 30 often correlates with sustained evictions.

jordan: From model/serving side, long seqs + int8 can blow up working set because of more KV entries per layer (we keep per-token KV). 45k tokens * N_layers ~= huge. If eviction churn happens, tail latency/backpressure follows. Two immediate mitigations: reduce max_context for that tenant OR enable prefix-only caching for their batch jobs.

sam: Can you also post the per-tenant rate pattern? We want to know if it's a noisy neighbor causing cross-tenant pressure vs their own workload.

alyssa: Per-tenant qps for last 30m: acme-prod bursts with 2-3 concurrent long jobs every 2-3 mins. Other tenants on dp-4 are low/normal. Looks like acme is the main driver.

mike: Ok cool. If it's single-tenant heavy, options: 1) move acme to an isolated slot on Dedicated (short term), 2) increase kv_cache reserved for that tenant, 3) enable aggressive compaction heuristics in the runtime (risk: slight CPU bump).

ops-bot: Note: autoscaler did not trigger for dp-4 in last hour (min_nodes cap=4). Autoscale events: none.

jordan: One more datapoint — we saw similar evict patterns where fragmentation prevented reclaimed slabs from being reused, yielding many small free/alloc cycles. There's a runtime flag `--kv-compact-interval=30s` vs default 5m. Lowering helps at cost of CPU.

alyssa: I spun up a repro script and ran ~10 synthetic long requests sequentially against their tenant; I hit 429s after ~6 requests. Collecting the kernel logs and runtime evict trace now.

alyssa: Repro script (trimmed):
```
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.redwood/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large-int8","input":"<45k tokens>","max_tokens":1024}' >/dev/null &
  sleep 2
done
```

mike: Good repro. Can you capture `/var/log/redwood/runtime.log` around the 429s and grep for `kv_eviction` and `alloc_fail`? Also run `pmap` on the process to see heap fragmentation.

sam: I'm going to open an internal ticket to escalate to eng-infra with logs + metrics + repro steps (INC-4321). I'll also propose a customer-facing workaround: reduce their max_context to 16k for now or move to a single-tenant slot.

alyssa: Customer is OK with a short config change if it keeps production stable.

jordan: Longer-term: we should add a tenant-level long-context throttle that prevents >N concurrent >X-token requests. Also add a runtime compaction mode that can be enabled per-pool. I'll sketch a design.

mike: For immediate action I'm going to: 1) enable `--kv-compact-interval=30s` on one node in dp-4, 2) temporarily bump kv_cache_reserved for acme to 4GB, 3) monitor evict rate for 30m.

ops-bot: Change request applied to node host-47: `--kv-compact-interval=30s`. KV_reserved for tenant acme-prod set to 4GB.

alyssa: After the change: evict_rate down from 3.2/s -> 0.6/s within 6 minutes; 429s subsided but still seeing a few tail spikes.

sam: Filing customer advisory: "We've applied temporary mitigations (cache reservation + compaction). We're investigating root cause and will schedule a follow-up."

mike: Next steps: eng-infra to review allocator behavior for fragmentation, add stronger monitoring (fragmentation percent + reclaim efficiency), and consider a per-tenant long-ctx admission controller.

jordan: I'll add a design doc link in INC-4321 and propose a rollout plan for compaction and admission controls.

sam: Closing loop with customer and marking as escalated to eng-infra. I'll keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
